senses.definition: The programs and other instructions a computer uses to do its work.
senses.example: Drawing software can turn my finger movements into a colored line.

senses.definition: The Sun and the objects held near it by gravity, including planets, moons, comets, and asteroids. Systems around other stars are often called planetary systems.
senses.example: Earth is one of eight planets in our solar system.

senses.definition: A flow of tiny charged particles that keeps blowing outward from the Sun.
senses.example: The solar wind carries pieces of the Sun’s outer atmosphere out into space.

senses.definition: A kind of matter that keeps its own shape under ordinary conditions.
senses.example: Ice is a solid, but it can melt into liquid water.

senses.definition: Made of material all the way through, with no empty middle.
senses.example: The toy was carved from one solid piece of wood.

senses.definition: Firm or strong enough to stay steady.
senses.example: The table needed a solid base so it would not wobble.

senses.definition: Either of the two moments each year when a hemisphere tilts farthest toward or away from the Sun.
senses.example: Near the June solstice, summer days are longest in places north of the equator.

senses.definition: The amount of one substance that can dissolve in a certain amount of another under given conditions.
senses.example: Heat can change the solubility of sugar in water.

senses.definition: An even mixture formed when one substance dissolves in another.
senses.example: Stirring salt into water made a salt solution.

senses.definition: To find the answer to a question or a way to deal with a problem.
senses.example: We worked together to solve the puzzle.

senses.definition: In a way that is unknown, surprising, or hard to explain.
senses.example: Somehow the button ended up in my shoe.

senses.definition: A way to find objects or measure distance using sound, often under water.
senses.example: The crew used sonar to make a map of the seafloor.

senses.definition: After a short amount of time.
senses.example: The movie will start soon.

senses.definition: Hurting when you touch or move it.
senses.example: My feet were sore after the long walk.

senses.definition: A painful or damaged spot on the body.
senses.example: The scratch turned into a little sore that needed a bandage.

senses.definition: Feeling sad about what happened or wishing you had acted differently.
senses.example: I am sorry I left without saying goodbye.

senses.definition: To put things into groups that share a feature or belong together.
senses.example: Please sort the pieces by color first.

senses.definition: A kind or type of something.
senses.example: This sort of paper is good for folding.

senses.definition: Putting things into a useful order or groups, such as from smallest to largest.
senses.example: Sorting the cards made it easier to find the number I wanted.

senses.definition: Vibrations that travel through material such as air, water, or a wall and can often be heard.
senses.example: The sound of the bell reached us from across the playground.

senses.definition: To make a noise or to seem a certain way to someone who hears you.
senses.example: You sound excited about your trip.

senses.definition: In good condition or based on good reasons.
senses.example: The builder checked that the old steps were sound.

senses.definition: Having the sharp taste of a lemon or vinegar.
senses.example: That green plum tasted sour.

senses.definition: To become or make something taste sour, or to become unpleasant.
senses.example: Milk may sour if left out for too long.

senses.definition: The direction opposite north, to your right if you face east.
senses.example: The birds flew south before winter.

senses.definition: Toward the direction opposite north.
senses.example: We drove south along the coast.

senses.definition: An area with room for something to fit or happen.
senses.example: Leave a space between each name on the list.

senses.definition: The huge area beyond Earth’s air, where planets, stars, and other objects are found.
senses.example: The telescope helps us see far into space.

senses.definition: To place things apart with gaps in between.
senses.example: Space the seedlings a hand’s width apart.

senses.definition: Extra and available in case it is needed.
senses.example: I keep a spare pencil in my backpack.

senses.definition: To give some time or resources away, or to do without part of them.
senses.example: Can you spare a minute to hold the door?

senses.definition: To keep someone or something from harm or trouble.
senses.example: We hoped the new fence would spare the flowers from hungry rabbits.

senses.definition: A tiny flash or glowing piece that comes from fire, friction, or an electrical jump.
senses.example: One spark rose from the campfire and went out.

senses.definition: To cause something to begin or happen.
senses.example: That picture may spark an idea for your story.

senses.definition: To use your voice to say words. It can also mean being able to use a language.
senses.example: She spoke slowly so the whole class could follow.

senses.definition: To talk louder so people can hear.
senses.example: Please speak up so the class at the back can hear the question.

senses.definition: To say what you think matters, especially when you might feel shy about it.
senses.example: When her partner was left out, Kelly decided to speak up.

senses.definition: Different from what is usual, or important to someone for a particular reason.
senses.example: We saved the big table for a special dinner.

senses.definition: Something offered for a limited time or for a particular purpose.
senses.example: The lunch special included a bowl of soup and toast.

senses.definition: A group of living things of the same kind. Members of many species can have young with one another, though scientists also use other clues to tell species apart.
senses.example: The blue whale and the humpback whale are different species.

senses.definition: Words spoken aloud to a group, often after planning what to say.
senses.example: I practiced my short speech about the playground.

senses.definition: The act or way of speaking.
senses.example: I could hear a little laughter in her speech as she told the story.

senses.definition: To pay out money for something.
senses.example: I saved a few coins to spend at the book sale.

senses.definition: To use time doing something or being somewhere.
senses.example: We spend an hour at the pool on Fridays.

senses.definition: A round three-dimensional shape with every point on its surface the same distance from its center.
senses.example: The ball was almost a perfect sphere.

senses.definition: To flow or fall out of a container or cause something to do so.
senses.example: Take small steps so you do not spill the water.

senses.definition: An amount that came out of its container and spread.
senses.example: The juice spill reached the edge of the table.

senses.definition: To turn around and around.
senses.example: The top will spin longer on a smooth table.

senses.definition: To twist fibers together to make yarn or thread.
senses.example: The craft teacher showed us how to spin wool.

senses.definition: A turn or a time spent moving around.
senses.example: We took the repaired wagon for a spin.

senses.definition: The part of a wash when the machine spins clothes fast to remove much of the water.
senses.example: The towels still felt damp after the spin cycle.

senses.definition: A thick bundle of nerve tissue protected by the backbone that carries many messages between the brain and body.
senses.example: Signals that help move your foot can travel through your spinal cord.

senses.definition: The energy, courage, or cheerfulness someone shows.
senses.example: Our team kept its spirit even after losing the first game.

senses.definition: In some beliefs or stories, a being or part of a person understood to exist without a body.
senses.example: In the tale, a spirit guards the old tree.

senses.definition: To make something less enjoyable or useful, or to become unfit to eat.
senses.example: Keep leftovers cold so they do not spoil.

senses.definition: To give someone so much of what they want that they stop expecting to wait or share.
senses.example: Grandpa jokes that he will spoil us with dessert before dinner.

senses.definition: A tiny cell that can grow into a new living thing in suitable conditions.
senses.example: A fern released spores from spots under its leaves.

senses.definition: A small mark that is different in color from what is around it.
senses.example: My dog has a white spot above one eye.

senses.definition: A particular place.
senses.example: We found a good spot to watch the sunset.

senses.definition: To see or notice something, often after looking for it.
senses.example: Can you spot the tiny frog in the grass?

senses.definition: To open something out, cover a larger area, or make something move from place to place.
senses.example: We spread the picnic blanket on the grass.

senses.definition: A soft food that you put on bread or crackers.
senses.example: The toast tasted good with a berry spread.

senses.definition: A computer table where you can organize values and use calculations based on them.
senses.example: My spreadsheet added all the numbers in the last column.

senses.definition: The season after winter and before summer.
senses.example: In spring, the garden filled with new green leaves.

senses.definition: A piece of material, often shaped like a coil, that returns to its shape after being pushed or pulled.
senses.example: The spring makes the door close when I let go.

senses.definition: A place where water comes naturally out of the ground.
senses.example: Water flowed from the spring into a small pool.

senses.definition: To jump, move, or come up suddenly.
senses.example: The cat likes to spring from the floor to the windowsill.

senses.definition: A wheel with teeth that fit into openings in a chain.
senses.example: The pedals turn a sprocket that pulls the bicycle chain.

senses.definition: A flat shape with four equal sides and four right angles.
senses.example: We divided the square into four smaller squares.

senses.definition: An open public space in a town or city, often surrounded by buildings.
senses.example: The farmer set up a stall in the town square.

senses.definition: To multiply a number by itself.
senses.example: To square five, multiply five by five.

senses.definition: A number you get by multiplying a whole number by itself.
senses.example: Thirty-six is a square number because six times six is 36.

senses.definition: The number zero or greater named by the square root symbol. Multiplying it by itself gives the number under the symbol.
senses.example: The square root of 49 is seven.

senses.definition: To press firmly from two or more sides.
senses.example: Squeeze the lemon over the bowl to get its juice.

senses.definition: To get through or fit into a tight space.
senses.example: Only one person can squeeze past the desk at a time.

senses.definition: A colored mark that is hard to remove.
senses.example: A drip of juice left a purple stain on my shirt.

senses.definition: To leave a mark or change a material’s color.
senses.example: The carpenter will stain the wood a darker shade.

senses.definition: A pointed stick or post driven into the ground.
senses.example: We tied the tomato plant to a stake.

senses.definition: Something you might gain or lose depending on what happens.
senses.example: Our class had a stake in the vote because we used the garden every day.

senses.definition: A mineral formation that grows downward from the roof of a cave as water leaves material behind.
senses.example: A drop hung for a moment at the tip of a stalactite.

senses.definition: A mineral formation that grows upward from a cave floor as water drops leave material behind.
senses.example: The rounded stalagmite grew where drops hit the same spot.

senses.definition: A small mark, printed label, or tool that makes a mark, such as one showing postage is paid.
senses.example: I put a stamp on the envelope before mailing it.

senses.definition: To press a mark onto something or bring your foot down hard.
senses.example: Please stamp your boots on the mat to knock the snow off.

senses.definition: To stay upright on your feet.
senses.example: We stood at the fence to watch the parade.

senses.definition: A frame or base that holds an object up.
senses.example: The music stand held the pages at the right height.

senses.definition: A small place where people sell or hand out things.
senses.example: A roadside stand sold baskets of berries.

senses.definition: A group of lines in a poem, often separated from other lines by an empty space.
senses.example: The poem had two stanzas of four lines each.

senses.definition: A huge ball of hot gas in space that gives off its own light. The Sun is the nearest one to Earth.
senses.example: A star can look like a tiny point because it is so far away.

senses.definition: A shape with points sticking out from the center.
senses.example: We drew a five-pointed star on the card.

senses.definition: A person who is especially well known for performing or doing something.
senses.example: She became a basketball star.

senses.definition: To play one of the main parts in a show, film, or play.
senses.example: I hope to star in the school play someday.

senses.definition: A long chain of sugar units found in foods such as rice, flour, or potatoes.
senses.example: Starch in the potato can be broken into smaller sugars.

senses.definition: To look directly at something for a long time.
senses.example: We stared at the empty nest hoping a bird would return.

senses.definition: To surprise someone suddenly, often making them jump or stop what they are doing.
senses.example: A loud knock can startle the sleeping dog.

senses.definition: To suffer from a lack of food over time.
senses.example: Without enough food in winter, some wild animals may starve.

senses.definition: To be very hungry, used in everyday talk as an exaggeration.
senses.example: I was starving after the long swim and ready for supper.

senses.definition: The main physical forms matter can take, including solid, liquid and gas.
senses.example: Ice, liquid water and water vapor are three states of matter.

senses.definition: Electric charge that has collected somewhere rather than flowing steadily through a path.
senses.example: Static electricity made the balloon pull toward the wall.

senses.definition: Firm, even, or staying about the same.
senses.example: He kept a steady pace all the way up the hill.

senses.definition: To hold or make something firm so it does not move too much.
senses.example: I steadied the stack of papers while she tied it.

senses.definition: To take something that belongs to another person without permission.
senses.example: The character tried to steal the farmer’s apples.

senses.definition: In baseball or softball, to move safely to the next base while the ball is in play without help from a hit.
senses.example: The runner tried to steal second base.

senses.definition: Water as an invisible gas, often made when water boils. In everyday speech the visible mist made when that gas cools is also called steam.
senses.example: Steam from the boiling water cooled into a cloud of tiny drops.

senses.definition: To cook food in the hot vapor above boiling water.
senses.example: We steamed the carrots in a basket above the water.

senses.definition: Rising or falling at a sharp angle.
senses.example: We walked our bicycles up the steep street.

senses.definition: To leave something in hot or cold liquid so its flavor or other qualities pass into the liquid.
senses.example: We steeped the tea leaves in hot water.

senses.definition: To control where a vehicle, boat, or other thing moves.
senses.example: Hold the handlebars firmly to steer the bicycle.

senses.definition: A bull that has been made unable to father calves.
senses.example: A steer stood in the shade near the fence.

senses.definition: An upright carved slab or pillar, often put up to remember a person or event.
senses.example: The carved stele stood near an old grave.

senses.definition: The part of a plant that holds up leaves, flowers, or other parts and carries materials between them.
senses.example: A sunflower has a tall stem.

senses.definition: A movement of one foot when you stand or walk.
senses.example: I took a step back to see the whole picture.

senses.definition: A flat part of a stair that you place your foot on.
senses.example: Watch out for the broken step.

senses.definition: One action in a plan or a set of directions.
senses.example: The next step is to fold both corners toward the center.

senses.definition: To move by lifting and placing a foot.
senses.example: Step over the puddle so you do not get wet.

senses.definition: One action at a time, in order.
senses.example: Our coach showed us step by step how to serve the ball.

senses.definition: A thin piece of wood or another hard material.
senses.example: We used a stick to draw a line in the sand.

senses.definition: To stay attached or make something attach to another surface.
senses.example: The tape will stick better if the box is dry.

senses.definition: To push or put something into or through a space or material.
senses.example: Stick the sign in the ground beside the plants.

senses.definition: Hard to bend or move.
senses.example: The stiff cardboard held the picture upright.

senses.definition: Tight and hard to move comfortably, said of part of the body.
senses.example: My legs felt stiff after we sat in the car so long.

senses.definition: A picture or artwork showing objects such as fruit, cups, flowers, or books.
senses.example: Our still life showed three apples and a glass bowl.

senses.definition: To move a spoon or tool around in a mixture or liquid.
senses.example: Stir the soup so the rice does not stick to the bottom.

senses.definition: To begin to move a little or to wake up.
senses.example: The puppy began to stir when I opened the door.

senses.definition: A small loop or line of thread used to hold fabric together.
senses.example: One stitch came out of my pocket.

senses.definition: To join or repair something by sewing it.
senses.example: Can you stitch the button back onto my coat?

senses.definition: A tiny opening in a plant surface. Water vapor and gases move through it.
senses.example: A microscope showed each stoma on the underside of the leaf.

senses.definition: The part of your body that holds food after you swallow it and mixes it with juices.
senses.example: Food moves from the stomach into the small intestine.

senses.definition: To walk or bring your foot down with heavy steps.
senses.example: We heard the muddy boots stomp down the porch steps.

senses.definition: A part or place that keeps information for the computer to use later.
senses.example: The picture was saved in storage and still appeared after I restarted.

senses.definition: A place that sells goods to people.
senses.example: We stopped at the store for bread.

senses.definition: To put something away so it can be found or used later.
senses.example: We store winter hats in the bottom drawer.

senses.definition: A time of rough weather, often with strong wind, rain, snow, or thunder.
senses.example: We brought the chairs inside before the storm.

senses.definition: To move somewhere suddenly and angrily.
senses.example: She nearly stormed out before remembering to explain why she was upset.

senses.definition: An account of something that happened or a tale someone made up.
senses.example: My friend told a funny story about a goat.

senses.definition: A level or floor of a building.
senses.example: The library reading room is on the second story.

senses.definition: Following one direction without a curve or bend.
senses.example: We drew a straight line through two dots.

senses.definition: In a direct way without turning aside or stopping elsewhere.
senses.example: Walk straight to the steps after you pass the gate.

senses.definition: A narrow stretch of water that connects two larger bodies of water.
senses.example: The ship crossed the strait between the two islands.

senses.definition: Unusual, unfamiliar, or hard to explain.
senses.example: We heard a strange clicking noise above us.

senses.definition: A person you do not know.
senses.example: We asked a stranger at the information desk for directions.

senses.definition: More unusual or unexpected. This is a form of strange.
senses.example: The ending was even stranger than the beginning.

senses.definition: A narrow strip of strong material used to carry, hold, or fasten something.
senses.example: One strap on my backpack was twisted.

senses.definition: To fasten or hold something with a strip of strong material.
senses.example: We strapped our bags to the back of the bike.

senses.definition: A small, flowing body of water.
senses.example: We crossed the stream on a wooden bridge.

senses.definition: To watch or listen to digital material as it arrives over a network.
senses.example: We streamed the school concert from home.

senses.definition: To flow in a long line or in large amounts.
senses.example: Sunlight streamed through the open doors.

senses.definition: A shallow spot where running water ripples over rocks or gravel.
senses.example: The stream riffle made a soft rushing sound under the bridge.

senses.definition: To pull or become longer or wider, or to reach your arms or legs out.
senses.example: Stretch the band gently so it does not snap.

senses.definition: A length or part of an area or of time.
senses.example: A long stretch of beach lay beyond the rocks.

senses.definition: To hit something with force.
senses.example: The mallet will strike the bell.

senses.definition: To come suddenly to someone’s mind.
senses.example: An idea can strike when you are thinking about something else.

senses.definition: A time when workers act together by stopping work to ask for a change.
senses.example: A train workers’ strike delayed several trips.

senses.definition: A thin cord made of twisted threads.
senses.example: I tied a piece of string around the package.

senses.definition: A stretched cord or wire on an instrument that makes sound when played.
senses.example: One guitar string broke during practice.

senses.definition: To put things onto or hang them from a cord.
senses.example: We strung paper shapes across the doorway.

senses.definition: A long, narrow piece of something.
senses.example: I tore a strip of paper to mark my page.

senses.definition: To take the covering or parts off something.
senses.example: We used a tool to strip loose paint from the old bench.

senses.definition: A repeated movement or set of movements used in an activity such as swimming or rowing.
senses.example: The swimmer practiced the breaststroke kick as part of a new stroke.

senses.definition: To try hard to do something difficult or to get free.
senses.example: I used to struggle with tying my shoelaces.

senses.definition: A time of great effort to do something hard.
senses.example: It was a struggle to push the cart up the hill.

senses.definition: Unwilling to change what you think or do, even when others give good reasons.
senses.example: We were stubborn about going our own way until the trail ended.

senses.definition: Hard to move, change, or get rid of.
senses.example: A stubborn mark remained after I washed the shirt.

senses.definition: To spend time learning about or looking carefully at something.
senses.example: We studied the footprints for clues about the animal.

senses.definition: A careful look at a subject or question to learn more about it.
senses.example: Our study of the pond lasted all spring.

senses.definition: Things or material whose names are not needed or known right now.
senses.example: Please move your stuff off the chair.

senses.definition: To fill a space tightly or push something into a space.
senses.example: We stuffed old newspapers into the empty boots.

senses.definition: To trip or almost fall while moving.
senses.example: I stumbled on a stone but caught my balance.

senses.definition: To find or meet something by chance, usually followed by on or upon.
senses.example: We stumbled upon an old trail behind the barn.

senses.definition: Strong and able to stand up to weight, use, or bumps.
senses.example: We packed the books in a sturdy box.

senses.definition: A way of doing, making, or showing something.
senses.example: The artist painted each animal in a playful style.

senses.definition: To arrange, shape, or design how something looks.
senses.example: I styled my costume to look like an old stage outfit.

senses.definition: The person or thing someone is talking, reading, or learning about.
senses.example: Weather was the subject of our class project.

senses.definition: The part of a sentence that tells who or what the verb is about.
senses.example: In “The lake froze,” the subject is “the lake.”

senses.definition: To cause someone or something to experience something, often unpleasant or demanding.
senses.example: The test subjected the tent to strong wind and heavy rain.

senses.definition: To reach a goal or do what you tried to do.
senses.example: We succeeded in building a tower that could hold five books.

senses.definition: To take someone’s place in a job or position after they leave.
senses.example: A new captain will succeed her at the end of the season.

senses.definition: A flexible cup that holds to a surface because air or water pushes harder on its outside than on the area under it.
senses.example: The suction cup held a little hook on the smooth glass.

senses.definition: Happening quickly and without warning.
senses.example: A sudden gust lifted the map off the bench.

senses.definition: A word part added at the end of a word or word part. It can change the meaning or how a word works in a sentence.
senses.example: Adding the suffix -less to care makes careless.

senses.definition: The right to vote in an election.
senses.example: Supporters of women’s suffrage worked for women to be able to vote.

senses.definition: To offer an idea or plan for someone to think about.
senses.example: I suggested that we move the picnic under the trees.

senses.definition: To give a clue that something may be true.
senses.example: The tracks suggest that a rabbit visited the garden.

senses.definition: A set of clothes made to be worn together, usually a jacket and matching pants or skirt.
senses.example: My uncle wore a dark suit to the party.

senses.definition: One of the four groups of standard playing cards, such as hearts or clubs.
senses.example: In this game, match the suit of the card already on the table.

senses.definition: To be right, useful, or pleasing for someone or something.
senses.example: Will this time suit everyone in your group?

senses.definition: The amount you get when you add numbers together.
senses.example: The sum of four and seven is eleven.

senses.definition: An amount of money.
senses.example: The club saved a small sum for new balls.

senses.definition: The season after spring and before autumn, usually the warmest part of the year.
senses.example: In summer, we often eat supper outdoors.

senses.definition: A huge explosion of a star or of certain remains of a star.
senses.example: The supernova grew bright enough for astronomers to see from very far away.

senses.definition: An amount of something ready to be used when needed.
senses.example: We carried a supply of clean water for the trip.

senses.definition: To give or provide what someone needs.
senses.example: The library will supply the paper for our posters.

senses.definition: To hold something up or keep it in place.
senses.example: Two strong posts support the porch roof.

senses.definition: To help or encourage someone or something.
senses.example: We came to the concert to support our friend.

senses.definition: Something that holds another thing up, or help given to someone.
senses.example: The broken branch needed a support.

senses.definition: To think that something is likely or true even though you are not sure.
senses.example: I suppose they took the earlier bus.

senses.definition: To imagine that something is true so you can think about what would happen.
senses.example: Suppose we could hear colors instead of seeing them.

senses.definition: Certain that something is true or reliable.
senses.example: I was sure I had put the keys by the door.

senses.definition: Used to say yes or show that you agree.
senses.example: Sure, I can help carry the boxes.

senses.definition: A pulling effect at the surface of a liquid that makes its surface tend to shrink.
senses.example: Surface tension helped pull a drop of rain into a rounded shape.

senses.definition: Something unexpected or the feeling you have when it happens.
senses.example: The first snow was a surprise to everyone.

senses.definition: To do something unexpected or make someone feel that it is unexpected.
senses.example: We will surprise Grandma with a handmade card.

senses.definition: To be or move all around someone or something.
senses.example: Tall trees surround the small pond.

senses.definition: A set of questions used to find out how people think or act.
senses.example: We made a survey about how students get to school.

senses.definition: To look over or examine something carefully, or ask people the same set of questions.
senses.example: We climbed the hill to survey the land before choosing a route.

senses.definition: To stay alive or continue to exist after danger, hardship, or change.
senses.example: Only a few plants survived the early frost.

senses.definition: To think something may be true without knowing it for sure.
senses.example: I suspect the missing glove is under the seat.

senses.definition: A person who may have committed a crime, according to the people investigating it.
senses.example: The officers spoke with a suspect about the missing bike.

senses.definition: To move food, drink, or something else from your mouth down your throat.
senses.example: Take a small sip and swallow it before you speak.

senses.definition: A small bird that often catches insects while flying and has long, pointed wings.
senses.example: A swallow flew just above the pond.

senses.definition: To give someone one thing in return for another, or to switch what you are doing or using.
senses.example: We swapped pencils to try each other’s colors.

senses.definition: An exchange in which people trade things or jobs.
senses.example: The book swap filled three shelves with new choices.

senses.definition: To move gently back and forth or from side to side.
senses.example: The grass swayed in the breeze.

senses.definition: To affect what someone thinks or chooses.
senses.example: My friend’s description might sway me to try the book.

senses.definition: To move dust or small things using a brush or broom.
senses.example: We swept the sand off the steps.

senses.definition: To move quickly, widely, or in a smooth curved motion.
senses.example: The spotlight swept across the room.

senses.definition: Having a taste like sugar.
senses.example: The pear tasted sweet when it was ripe.

senses.definition: Kind, pleasing, or gentle.
senses.example: It was sweet of you to save me a seat.

senses.definition: To grow larger or puff up.
senses.example: The bread dough began to swell as it rose.

senses.definition: A slow rise and fall of water in the sea.
senses.example: A gentle swell lifted our boat.

senses.definition: Moving or happening quickly.
senses.example: A swift current carried the leaf under the bridge.

senses.definition: A bird with long, narrow wings that spends much of its time flying and catching insects.
senses.example: A swift swooped over the roof.

senses.definition: To move through water by moving your body, legs, fins, or arms.
senses.example: The ducks swam across the pond in a line.

senses.definition: To move back and forth or around a point that stays fixed.
senses.example: I watched the gate swing open.

senses.definition: A seat hanging from ropes or chains that can move back and forth.
senses.example: We took turns on the swing.
